tasks.title: MessageToFutureSelf + BullMQ worker database authority
tasks.evidence: MessageToFutureSelf is registered in DIRECT_DB_MODELS with all three mapper exits; the letter list and the create path go through SelfPersistenceService, the store getter throws, and the two legacy array mutations are guarded. Create writes the letter and its follow-up job in one transaction with the context reference validated for ownership inside it. Design A6: the notification consent is read from the database inside the claim transaction and the notification row is written in that same transaction, so "delivered with no notification" can only mean consent was off; a duplicate delivery short-circuits on the conditional claim and writes nothing. A bounded reconciler re-enqueues durable pending jobs at startup and every five minutes. batch3-future-self-authority.spec.ts 8/8; batch1-usernotification.spec.ts 7/7 (incl. the A6 rollback case); mutations M45, M46, M47 PROVEN.

tasks.title: Known-ID impersonation: the identity header is not authentication
tasks.evidence: Superseded the signed-token version: a signature cannot be revoked, so a lost device stayed usable for the whole TTL. The credential is now <sessionId>.<secret> with only sha256(secret) stored, verified by a database lookup, so two instances agree without a shared cache and a restart loses nobody. Expiry, per-device revocation and rotation all work; rotation revokes its predecessor in the same transaction. Verification is async, so an Express middleware resolves it once per request and publishes it through AsyncLocalStorage rather than making ~96 synchronous ownership helpers async (a missing await there silently disables the check - it happened once already with the privacy gates). Migration 20261009000000_anonymous_session; the 12 baseline migrations are untouched. batch3-identity-credential.spec.ts 16/16 including restart survival, two-instance agreement and cross-instance revocation; batch3-identity-matrix.spec.ts 27/27; mutations M40-M44, M48, M49 PROVEN. mp app stores the credential through Capacitor Preferences on native and awaits the identity before every request.
tasks.nextAction: Independent security review. Two things a reviewer must weigh: there is still no keystore-backed storage on native (see docs/architecture/IDENTITY_CREDENTIAL_STORAGE.md), and historical account recovery has no verifiable binding (B3-R11-HISTORICAL).

tasks.title: Product change: a fresh client now gets a new empty identity instead of the demo user
tasks.evidence: Removing the demo fallback is inseparable from removing the impersonation hole: the app used to show the seeded demo content to every caller precisely because any caller could be the demo user. A new client now bootstraps an anonymous identity with no content (verified live: 0 letters against the demo identity's 5). The seeded demo experience is preserved for local work by ALLOW_DEMO_IDENTITY=true on the server and VITE_USE_DEMO_IDENTITY=true on the client, both off by default.

tasks.title: A failing follow-up job was invisible: only connection errors were logged
tasks.evidence: The worker logged the Redis client "error" event but not BullMQ job failures, so a job that threw was retried and then dropped with nothing in the log. Found while diagnosing a regression this session: the job id and error message are now logged (the payload is not, because it can carry the user's own text).

tasks.title: Historical anonymous accounts have no verifiable binding, so they cannot be handed back
tasks.evidence: Before this change the C-end had no authentication at all: the header was a bare user id and nothing about a caller was ever verified. There is therefore no stored evidence that could prove who an existing anonymous account belonged to, and issuing a session for a user id on request would recreate the exact hole just closed. No path does this today: a session is only issued for a user the server has just created, or for the demo user under an explicit flag.
tasks.nextAction: Needs a product decision plus a verifiable channel (a real WeChat openid login, or a recovery code issued while the old client was still trusted). Do NOT auto-transfer an existing account to whoever names its id.
